tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__edit_version
tools.description: Publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit (some clients refuse any artifact but your own as owner-only), by replacing text in its current document: use it for a small change instead of sending the whole page to publish_version. The server reads the live index.html, applies every edit in order, and publishes the result as one new version; if any edit cannot be applied, nothing is published. Each old_text must occur exactly once in the document as it stands when that edit is applied: include enough surrounding text to make it unique. base_version must name the live version (from get_artifact, read_artifact, list_files or your last publish result); if it is no longer live the call is rejected with a conflict that names the live version: read what you are changing again and retry. To rename the artifact pass title, which also rewrites the document's <title> element; an edit to that element without title is refused, because the server keeps it in step with the artifact's title. Artifacts that contain a live (collaboratively edited) document cannot be edited here. An artifact made from a type is edited only if this server offers list_files, and only with path: one of its own text files, as list_files lists them, never its page or its type's files.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_files
tools.description: Publish an artifact from files on disk: their bytes go from the files to the artifact and do not pass through you. Prefer this to publish_version when the page's files already exist, when there is more than one file or an image, or when the page is large. For each file give `as`, the path it is served at, and `path`, its absolute path on the machine where your own file tools run; leave `uri` out. index.html is required in a new artifact. Limits for one call: 256 files, 20 MiB a file, 64 MiB in all. The client may refuse a file it will not send, such as a secrets file, a link or a path outside the working folder. Omit slug to create an artifact, private to you. To republish, give slug and base_version (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish); title and icon are kept when omitted. A republish changes only the files named and keeps the rest, which stay served: to take a file away, list it in remove. mode "replace" makes the files named the whole artifact and drops the rest. This tool publishes only to an artifact of yours. **Files Claude did not write**: Claude reads the whole file before publishing it, even when the person asks it not to. Publishing distributes the content, and Claude never distributes what it has not seen. A request for privacy is a reason to read before publishing, not an exemption. If Claude cannot read the file, it does not publish it. **Claude never publishes** a page that impersonates a real person or organization, for example by using their name, branding, byline or domain. Claude also never publishes fabricated records, receipts or reviews presented as genuine, forms or flows that collect credentials or payment details under false pretenses, or content that targets a private individual. Claude refuses whether it wrote the page or the person supplied it, and whatever purpose is claimed, such as a prop or a test, when the page would work as the real thing. If publishing is refused, Claude does not suggest other ways to host or share the page.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version. Leave it out to keep the current one.

slug.description: The artifact's slug. Omit to create a new artifact.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
tools.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

schema.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__publish_version
schema.description: Publish an artifact: either create a new artifact — omit slug and give title and content; you become its owner and it starts private to you — or publish a new version of an artifact you own, or of one in your organization that you can edit — give slug and base_version. Some clients may publish only to your own artifacts: there the call is refused as owner-only. Republishing is read-then-send: base_version must name the live version you are replacing (from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result) — if it is no longer live, the publish is rejected with a conflict; re-read and retry from the current state. On success the new version goes live immediately. When republishing, the artifact's stored connectors manifest carries forward unchanged, and so do title, favicon, icon and contract when omitted. Content is capped at 16 MiB.

artifact_title.description: The artifact's current title, as get_artifact gives it. Needed when shared_live is 'public'.

base_version.description: Required when slug is given: the version id this publish replaces — echo the version get_artifact or read_artifact returned (or your last publish result's). Rejected with a conflict if it no longer names the live version, so concurrent edits are never silently overwritten. Omit when creating.

content.description: The complete HTML document, at most 16 MiB. Must sniff as text/html — begin it with <!DOCTYPE html>.

contract.description: Optional runtime-contract version (MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH). Leave it out to keep the current one. Pass one only when the user asks for a different version, or this server's answer says to. If the publish is rejected because the contract is yanked or out of the supported window, republish with an explicit "0.0.0" to clear the contract — omitting the argument is not a reliable recovery (the server may carry the stored contract forward, repeating the rejection).

deadline.description: Optional, rarely needed: by when pages still open on an OLDER version must have moved to this one — one word: now, 15m, 1h, 24h, 7d, or an ISO-8601 time at most 30 days ahead. Omit it for ordinary edits (open pages then move at their next quiet moment); it cannot be relaxed once published.

favicon.description: Optional legacy emoji marker; omit it.

icon.description: One short, generic word for the artifact's tab icon — a plain signifier of what it is, such as chart, calendar, recipe, code or map; not a product or brand name. Pass one when creating; omit when republishing to keep the current icon.

shared_live.description: States who the artifact you are republishing is already shared with, and changes nothing: its 'read' value from get_artifact, read_artifact or your last publish result. Required when that value is 'users' (named people or groups), 'org' (the user's whole organization) or 'public' (anyone with the link). Leave it out for a new artifact and when the value is 'owner'. Rejected if it does not match the artifact's current value.

slug.description: The artifact's server-assigned slug (UUID), e.g. from list_artifacts, get_artifact or the artifact's own URL. Omit to create a new artifact.

title.description: Browser-tab title. Required when creating. When republishing it is optional — omitted, the new version keeps the current live version's title (the server also keeps the stored HTML's <title> element in sync with it); pass a value only to rename the artifact, never invent a new title on a routine republish.

tools.name: mcp__claude-artifacts__read_artifact
tools.description: Read the current document of an artifact: one that the user owns, or one that belongs to someone in the user's organization and that the user can open. Read a pasted claude.ai artifact link with this tool. Returns a JSON summary (slug, version id, title, favicon, runtime-contract version, total_lines, and for a multi-file artifact its file names), then the HTML of the version the user is served, then a reminder. The HTML, and the summary's title, favicon and file names, are wrapped in an <untrusted-document-...> tag that the summary's notice names; the tag is not part of them. A document over ~1 MiB is not served whole: read it in parts with offset and limit, which count lines; next_offset says where the next part starts. # Browser Use

Direct browser control via CDP. For task-specific edits, use `agent-workspace/agent_helpers.py`. For setup, install, or connection problems, read https://github.com/browser-use/browser-harness/blob/main/install.md.

## When Not to Use

A basic fetch of public information needs no browser. If a plain HTTP request can read it — a public page, an API, docs — use `curl` or your fetch tool, and leave the browser alone. Use browser-use when the task needs interaction (click, type, navigate), the user's logged-in session, JS rendering, or a bot-protected page. If a direct fetch fails or returns a shell page, then escalate to the browser.

Domain skills are off by default. Set `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` to enable them; see the bottom section.

**If `BH_DOMAIN_SKILLS=1` and the task is site-specific, read every file in the matching `$BH_AGENT_WORKSPACE/domain-skills/<site>/` directory before inventing an approach.**

## Usage

```bash
browser-use <<'PY'
print(page_info())
PY
```

- Invoke as `browser-use`. Use heredocs for multi-line commands.
- Helpers are pre-imported. `run.py` calls `ensure_daemon()` before `exec`.
- First navigation for a task is `new_tab(url)`, not `goto_url(url)`. The daemon
  preserves the attached tab across separate CLI invocations, so do not call
  `new_tab()` again in every script.
- Keep one working tab per task/site. Before opening another, inspect
  `current_tab()` and `list_tabs()` and use `switch_tab()` to reuse a matching
  tab. Do not leave duplicate tabs on the same URL or close tabs you did not
  create.
- At task completion, close tabs created for the task that are no longer needed.
  Keep a tab open if the user needs to see it, it is needed for a known follow-up,
  or closing it could discard unsaved work or other important state.
- `new_tab()` and `switch_tab()` attach and move the horse marker without
  changing Chrome's visible tab. Screenshots and normal CDP input work in the
  background. Never call `activate_tab(target)` automatically: it brings Chrome
  to the foreground. Call it only when the user explicitly asks to see or
  visibly switch to that tab. Do not pair `switch_tab()` with `activate_tab()`.
- A local daemon is a connection to the whole Chrome instance, not to one site,
  task, card, or agent. Omit `BU_NAME` and reuse the default daemon for normal
  sequential local work across websites, tabs, screenshots, and Codex turns.
  Do not invent per-job names such as `gmail1375` or `slack1371`: every new
  local daemon opens another browser-level CDP connection and Chrome may show
  another Allow prompt.
- Set `BH_TAB_MARKER=0` before starting the daemon to leave page titles unchanged.
  The horse marker remains enabled by default.
- A timeout or page that pauses while hidden is not permission to foreground
  Chrome. Keep using background CDP operations. For a focus-gated page,
  temporarily call `cdp("Emulation.setFocusEmulationEnabled", enabled=True)`,
  perform and verify the operation, then disable it in a `finally` block. If
  background control still cannot work, report that limitation instead of
  activating the tab. Do not invent a `Runtime.evaluate` scroll replacement or
  a cross-frame JS walker.
- The normal local flow attaches to the running Chrome/Chromium CDP endpoint. No browser ids or local profile selection.

## plugin:desktop-commander:desktop-commander
Desktop Commander provides tools for working with the user's authorized device.
- Filesystem tools handle direct file and directory operations within configured access boundaries.
- Terminal process tools support shell commands, REPLs, and long-running processes. start_process creates a process session; interact_with_process sends input; read_process_output reads later output; force_terminate ends a session.
- Search tools are session-based. start_search creates a search session; get_more_search_results reads its results; stop_search ends it early.
- Absolute paths are generally the most reliable because relative paths depend on the active working directory.
- allowedDirectories and each tool's schema, annotations, and documented constraints define the operational boundaries.

Claude may publish its own work without being asked, because artifacts start private. Claude builds those as files and lets the person decide whether they get a URL. When a finished piece of work is meant for other people or agents, such as a report for a team or the case for a decision the team has yet to make, Claude does not treat it as finished while it exists only in this conversation or in a local file. Claude publishes it and gives the person the link, so they have a private page ready to share when they choose. Claude publishes it even when the request is phrased as a question, such as "can you write up the plan?". **CR-1a. Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads that reach the simulation (H9); which files may read a clock at all is the allow-list owned by ADR-0010 `SIM-02`, not kept here *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*. **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16); (6) `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()`, the unconditional last step of the driver frame: `TickDriver.frame()` is a two-statement wrapper, `_frame_body(delta_us)` (steps 1 to 5, which may return early on a pause, a restore request, a fault or a zero-tick frame) and then `deliver_frame_end()`, with no statement after it, so no exit path skips frame-end delivery (ADR-0001 section 1, test KRN-FRAME-END) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*; what `deliver_frame_end()` delivers, and how `load_seq` and `deliver_all()` on `LOADING -> RUNNING` relate to it, is defined in CR-10 (**Frame-end delivery and the restore marker**) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix)*. **The accumulator is cleared on every transition into `RUNNING`** (from `LOADING`, `PAUSED` or `SAVING`), so a load, an autosave or a pause never produces catch-up ticks afterwards. The driver node has a process priority that runs it before the presentation nodes, so presentation reads the tick the driver just produced. **Step 0 — input sample, and the priority table** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: nothing in the driver's step list sampled input, so the best-case latency of D.4 rested on an unstated ordering. The order inside one rendered frame is now fixed by process priority (lower runs first): **(0)** the input adapter (an `INPUT_SURFACE` object; it reads the engine's input state for this frame and calls `submit`, so its commands are admitted before the boundary service and the tick loop); **(1)** the `TickDriver` node (boundary service, then the tick loop, then forgiveness, result flush, paused service, then `deliver_frame_end()`); **(1.5)** the host-service slot (`HOST_SERVICE`, `SaveHost` only: its per-frame poll runs after the driver and observes the last committed tick boundary; ADR-0006); **(2)** presentation (the single presentation host and its stages: Pixel-Perfect pipeline, HUD, Lighting, Audio), which read what the driver just committed. The ordinals 0, 1, (1.5) and 2 are order only; ADR-0001 section 2 fixes the values `INPUT_ADAPTER` -100, `TICK_DRIVER` -50, `HOST_SERVICE` -40 and `PRESENTATION` 0 *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*. The adapter's priority is therefore strictly below the driver's number; a presentation node must sort after both the driver and the host service (a lint on `process_priority` values plus ADR-0001's boot-time tree walk; the engine reference is silent on ordering between nodes, so the spike verifies it, KRN-LAT-02). Tests call `Kernel.step()` directly, or inject `delta_us` into the driver; nothing in the kernel sleeps or reads a clock. **Main thread and `Engine.time_scale`**: the kernel, the driver and every owner callable run on the main thread only — no worker thread calls `submit`, a read view or a mutator (a lint forbids `Thread`, `WorkerThreadPool` and `call_deferred` into kernel code); `_process(delta)`'s `delta` is scaled by `Engine.time_scale` in the engine's contract as we read it (the pinned engine reference does not state it — **[UNV]**, verify in the spike), so release builds pin `Engine.time_scale = 1.0` (a boot check records `TIME_SCALE_NON_UNIT` in diagnostics otherwise) and a dev build that changes it knowingly scales simulated speed through `delta` — ticks stay exact integers either way.

Subscriber handlers run with writes disabled. Render `PRESENTATION` gets no submit API; `INPUT_SURFACE` is the one class that may submit, which is how "presentation never writes simulation" coexists with menus that issue commands. *(The `INPUT_SURFACE` and `PROJECTOR` readings of the TD rule are provisional pending a technical-director ruling — Open Questions.)* **Sim never calls presentation**: the flow is always state → notification → presentation. Horror light disturbance and Attention flicker are state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting. There are two consumer channels: true values (Debug Overlay only) and filtered values (the Perception Filter reads true state and publishes what a client perceives; presentation nodes read the filtered channel). The kernel exposes `tick_alpha` for render interpolation; owners of moving state expose previous and current committed values in their read views. The transport is decided in ADR-0004: a kernel-owned registry, not signals; `subscribe` is per block on a class-bound facet, `subscribe(block_id, handler, name)` *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0004 sync)*. **Catch-up delivery** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; ratified 2026-10-27 — user ruling (design-review decisions), R-12, Open Question 21 resolved)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — user rulings)*: in a frame that runs more than one tick, `PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR` and `DIAGNOSTIC` batches are delivered once, at `deliver_frame_end()` (after the frame's last tick, forgiveness, the result flush and the paused service, not inside the loop; see **Frame-end delivery and the restore marker** below) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix)*, with `tick` = that tick and `change_keys` = the union of the frame's ticks (collapsing to `ALL` past `MAX_DIRTY_KEYS`), because presentation only ever reads the last committed state and N intermediate batches are wasted work; `INPUT_SURFACE`, `REPLICATION` and control-plane callers still receive every tick's batch, and the result buffer is flushed every tick. Ticks stay atomic (G6); only the delivery of a presentation batch is merged. **Delivery on an early exit from the loop** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: if the loop stops early (a P6 pause, a restore, a fault), the merged batch covers **committed ticks only** — the union of the `change_keys` of ticks whose P4 ran — and is delivered by `deliver_frame_end()`, which runs on every exit path (so after the state change is visible to the driver) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix)*; a fault delivers nothing for the faulting tick (P4 never ran) and merges nothing, and a restore delivers `ALL` for every block to every subscriber class (the world was replaced) once the kernel is `RUNNING` again, through `deliver_all()` (below).
**Frame-end delivery and the restore marker** *(New 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix; owners ADR-0001 sections 1 and 4, ADR-0004 sections 5 and 6, ADR-0009)*. (1) `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()` first applies deferred subscribe and unsubscribe changes, then closes (sorts) every frame buffer that received a union and delivers each dirty one to the `FRAME_MERGED` classes (`PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR`, `DIAGNOSTIC`), then clears them. It is the unconditional last step of `TickDriver.frame()` (CR-1a step 6) and runs exactly once on every exit path: a P6 pause, a restore request, a fault, a zero-tick frame and an ordinary frame (KRN-FRAME-END). The phrases "after the frame's last tick" and "at the exit" in this rule therefore mean "at `deliver_frame_end`", never from P5 and never at the end of the tick loop; `PER_TICK` classes (`INPUT_SURFACE`, `REPLICATION`) are still delivered from P5. (2) On every `LOADING -> RUNNING` transition (a restore and a new game) the kernel increments the read-only `PresentationClock.load_seq` and then, immediately after, calls `Kernel.deliver_all()`: it clears the tick and frame buffers and the event pool (a pending merged union does not survive a restore), then delivers one `ALL` batch per block to every subscriber class with `tick` = the restored `T`, and runs `snap_baseline` on entry to `RUNNING`. `load_seq` is incremented once per such transition and never on `PAUSED -> RUNNING` or `SAVING -> RUNNING`, so the increment precedes every `deliver_all` batch of that frame. `ChangeBatch` carries no load flag: a load-time `ALL` batch is indistinguishable from an overflow `ALL`, by design, and a presenter that must react differently to a restore (the Pixel-Perfect camera CUT) compares `load_seq` with the value it last saw. `PresentationClock` is the kernel-backed, read-only handle through which presentation reads `tick_alpha` and `load_seq`; it cannot write. A restore frame still runs 0 ticks (CR-1a), so the `deliver_all` batches arrive in the same frame's boundary service, and that frame's `deliver_frame_end` has nothing merged left to deliver. Tested by KRN-FRAME-END and KRN-LOAD-SEQ. **Subscriber lifetime** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `subscribe(class, handler)` returns a **subscription handle**; `handle.unsubscribe()` removes it, and the kernel also checks `handler.is_valid()` before each call and prunes a freed subscriber (counter `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, not an error and not `INCOMPLETE`), so a freed HUD or Chart Table node never raises an engine error that would be misreported. P5 iterates a **snapshot of the subscriber list taken before P5 begins**, so a handler that subscribes or unsubscribes during delivery affects the next tick only. `Kernel.dispose()` (idempotent) unsubscribes everything, drops the registries and breaks the `RefCounted` cycles between kernel, driver and handles, so a test kernel is freed deterministically (no leaked instances at test end).
- **KRN-FRAME-END** **GIVEN** a recording kernel behind a `TickDriver`, **WHEN** five frames run (a pause requested at tick 3 of 4; a fault at tick 2; a restore request; a zero-tick frame; an ordinary four-tick frame as control), **THEN** `deliver_frame_end` is reached exactly once in each of the five. (auto; injected delta) [CR-1a] *(New 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*
- **KRN-LOAD-SEQ** **GIVEN** a kernel with a presentation host reading `PresentationClock.load_seq`, **WHEN** a restore and a new game each complete `LOADING -> RUNNING`, and separately a `PAUSED -> RUNNING` and a `SAVING -> RUNNING` occur, **THEN** `load_seq` increases by exactly 1 on each of the first two, increases before the `deliver_all` batches of that frame are delivered, and is unchanged across the other two. (auto) [CR-1a, CR-15] *(New 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*

**CR-15. Control plane** (host-local, not commands): `request_pause`, `request_resume`, `request_snapshot`, `request_restore`, `request_new_game` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review; CR-18)*, `request_shutdown`, `request_bind_seat(peer_id, player_id)` and `request_unbind_seat(peer_id)` (the host-only writers of binding half (a), CR-7; the composition root calls `request_bind_seat(HOST_PEER_ID, 1)` as a boot step) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — ADR-0002 GDD sync)*. Callers: Save/Load, the pause/Chart Table UI (host-local call), boot code. **Timing** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*: a request is recorded when made — from any phase, from a hook, from a P5 handler, or from outside a tick (a UI call between frames) — and served at the **next boundary**, where a boundary is the P6 of a tick or the driver's per-frame boundary service (run before any tick of the frame and, while `PAUSED`, every frame), whichever comes first; the call itself never changes state. `request_shutdown` is accepted from **every state except `SHUTTING_DOWN`** (including `BOOTING`, `LOADING` and `SAVING`; in those it is served at the boundary that follows the atomic step). Requests reaching the same boundary are applied in arrival order, never coalesced: a `request_pause` then a `request_resume` on one boundary leaves the kernel `RUNNING` with no paused service cycle run; a caller that needs a definite state re-issues the state it wants (Chart Table CT-4) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from chart-table-web-map-and-menus (ASK-CT-9))*. **`request_restore(payload, restore_epoch, expected_state_hash, has_expected_hash)`** (K-4; `has_expected_hash` is a typed `bool` and `0` is a legal hash, so there is no sentinel value) *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0002 sync)* *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review, delegated ruling R1; amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R1 as amended by R13/R14: `restore_epoch` is supplied by Save/Load, whose epoch staging step has completed before the call is made: `EPOCH_DURABLE`, or a logged `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` with `save_status = FAILED`, or no advance was due. Save/Load advances the value on every death-stub restore, every `FAULT_RECOVERY` and every Continue except one of the newest non-demoted verified `QUIT` generation, which carries it unchanged and writes nothing (R13). The kernel never waits on that write: no Save/Load I/O completes inside `LOADING`, which stays atomic within one boundary service (States). **Listed exposure (failure path, R14):** after `SL_EPOCH_NOT_DURABLE` the installed epoch exists only in Save/Load's memory, so a process kill before Save/Load's next successful epoch write may replay that epoch once; G3/G4 are unaffected because they are defined given the `(save bytes, restore_epoch)` pair. The kernel holds it read-only for the session, exposes it in the `kernel.clock` read view (CR-8) and rejects a value outside the u32 range in its pre-check, `RESTORE_EPOCH_RANGE`)*: when `has_expected_hash` is true, the kernel recomputes `state_hash(PERSIST, T)` (D.12) after the last `post_restore()`, inside `LOADING` and before the first `RUNNING` tick, and reports the K-4 verdict `{T, computed_hash, verdict}` to the requester, `verdict` one of `MATCH`, `MISMATCH` or `NONE`; when `has_expected_hash` is false (the pre-K-4 release file case) the compare is skipped, `expected_state_hash` is ignored and the verdict is `NONE` *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0002 sync)*. Save/Load derives its EXACT / REBASED / mismatch verdict from it (SL-12). A mismatch is **not** a `FAULTED` transition — release plays on; policy is the requester's. Save/Load does not use restore-into-`PAUSED` for this window *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (K-4))*. **Control-plane read access:** a control-plane caller is not one of the CR-10 subscriber classes; Save/Load (the one such caller at MVP) may read `kernel.clock`, the Controller's per-seat `loco_state`, the Graph's `read_view.failures()` and an optional Attention `SIM` read view, reads those views by a once-per-frame poll (`SaveService.poll_frame` at `HOST_SERVICE` after the driver); it subscribes to nothing and receives no end-of-tick callback *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0006 sync)*; it never reads `PERCEPTION_OUT`, never submits commands and never holds a `WriteScope` *(Amended 2026-10-27 — consistency pass, routed from save-load-and-versioned-format (SL-13))*. In VS-B a guest's pause or save *request* is a command defined by Session or Save/Load, validated on the host, which then calls the control API.

**CR-16. Pause semantics.** `PAUSED` stops the tick but not rendering. While paused, submit accepts only types flagged `allowed_when_paused` by their owner, and **only non-diegetic actions may carry the flag** (save, settings, resume, menu navigation) — no gameplay verb that changes `SIM` state is allowed while paused, so a solo player cannot equip, repair or re-route with time stopped mid-tell (Dread Before Chaos), and solo pause behaves like co-op's overlay-only pause; a paused-allowed command may write only blocks registered `gameplay = false` **and** named in the type's `writes_blocks` (boot-checked, CR-6; the `WriteScope` issued in the paused cycle carries exactly that set, and a write outside it is refused and counted as `WRITE_OUTSIDE_SCOPE`), never a `SIM` gameplay block *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*; everything else is rejected `PAUSED` immediately, never queued, so there is no burst on resume. Admitted paused-allowed commands are dispatched by a **paused service cycle** that runs P1, P2, P4, P5 and P6 with no P3 and with `T` unchanged, **once per rendered frame while `PAUSED`** (the paused boundary, which also serves control-plane requests), so a save or a menu action takes effect without advancing simulated time. ### States and Transitions

**Kernel states**

| State | Meaning | Tick advancing | Accepts submit |
|-------|---------|----------------|----------------|
| `BOOTING` | Registries being populated (CR-6), then idle until the first accepted New campaign or Continue; the main menu and boot-flow screens run with the kernel in this state (Chart Table TX-30, EC-CT-37); nothing loaded *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`) |
| `LOADING` | Restoring a snapshot or building new-game state; also entered mid-session for reload, including the MVP death stub (Save/Load); entered from `BOOTING` by the first-boot `request_new_game` / `request_restore` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*. Atomic within one boundary service — it never spans a frame *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review)*. No wait on Save/Load I/O happens inside it: when a restore advances `restore_epoch`, Save/Load's `slot_epoch_a/b.bin` write completes (or is declared not durable) in a pre-restore staging step before `request_restore` is made, and a carried Continue writes nothing (CR-15) *(Amended 2026-10-28 — delegated ruling R14)*. Its last step is the CR-7 binding rebuild *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`) |
| `RUNNING` | Normal ticking | Yes | Yes |
| `PAUSED` | Single-player pause (CR-16) | No | Only `allowed_when_paused` types |
| `SAVING` | Snapshot capture at a tick boundary; atomic within a single boundary service (never spans a frame), returns to the prior state; control-plane requests made while it is active are `DEFERRED` (Control-plane request outcomes below) and applied in arrival order afterwards *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)* | No | No (`NOT_ACCEPTING`), as `LOADING`: a submit during `SAVING` can only come from inside a `snapshot()` or another boundary callback, which the contract already forbids from having side effects, and admitting it would contradict the `PAUSED` rule when the save returns to `PAUSED`; it is rejected, counted as a violation (`SUBMIT_DURING_SAVING`, CR-19(d)) *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* |
| `FAULTED` | A fault reported through the fault channel (CR-19) by any kernel-invoked owner callable — `apply`, `validate`, a hook, `snapshot`, `restore`, `post_restore`, `init_world`, `default_state`, `binding_source` *(Amended 2026-10-28 — cross-GDD fix)*, `commit_baseline` or `snap_baseline` — in `RUNNING`, in the `PAUSED` service cycle, in `SAVING` or in `LOADING` (a `read_view` fault is recorded and returns an empty view; it never faults the kernel, CR-19(a)); a restore failure; or a boot failure after registration. Never requested *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)* | No | No |

`FAULTED` exists because CR-9's "apply cannot fail" contract needs somewhere for a reported fault to go other than undefined behaviour. In `FAULTED` the kernel never writes or autosaves over an existing save; a dev build halts with diagnostics, release returns to the menu.

Tick driver, clock source and catch-up** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — design review; closes former Open Question 2, the technical-director confirms it in the spike)*. `Kernel.step()` has no clock. A `TickDriver` (a `RefCounted`, no scene tree) owns the accumulator, receives time as an injected integer count of microseconds (`delta_us`), and is driven by exactly one node with `process_mode = PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS` from its `_process(delta)`; that node converts the engine's `delta` to `delta_us` once, and that conversion plus the diagnostics timer are the only wall-clock reads that reach the simulation (H9); which files may read a clock at all is the allow-list owned by ADR-0010 `SIM-02`, not kept here *(Amended 2026-10-29 — ADR-0001 sync)*. **Godot's physics step is not the clock**: at MVP the avatar has no physics body (CR-13), so nothing needs the physics callback, and the driver needs no coupling to `physics/common/max_physics_steps_per_frame` (the former coupled constraint 4 is deleted). A later Vertical Slice physics projection runs in `_physics_process` as a `PROJECTOR` reading committed state and never steps the kernel. The accumulator is an integer in units of *microseconds × TICK_RATE*, so one tick is exactly `TICK_UNITS` = 1,000,000 units for every integer `TICK_RATE` (no float drift, no boundary flips); each frame that begins (after the boundary service) with the kernel `RUNNING` adds `acc += delta_us × TICK_RATE`. **Order of the add against the clear** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: the boundary service runs first; if it moved the kernel into `RUNNING` (a resume, a load, a finished save) the accumulator is cleared and **that frame's own `delta_us` is discarded** — the frame runs 0 ticks, because its wall time was spent paused, loading or saving — and the add applies from the next frame on; a frame that finds the kernel not `RUNNING` adds nothing. Per frame the driver (1) runs the boundary service (CR-15) before any tick; (2) while the kernel is `RUNNING`, runs `step()` `ticks_run = min(floor(acc / TICK_UNITS), MAX_TICKS_PER_FRAME)` times, **re-reading the kernel state after every `step()`** and stopping (and clearing `acc`) the moment it is no longer `RUNNING` — a P6 pause, a restore, a fault; (3) applies lag forgiveness (D.5); (4) flushes the result buffer (CR-5); (5) while `PAUSED`, runs the paused boundary service (CR-16); (6) `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()`, the unconditional last step of the driver frame: `TickDriver.frame

+Subscriber handlers run with writes disabled. Horror light disturbance and Attention flicker are state that Lighting reads, not calls into Lighting. There are two consumer channels: true values (Debug Overlay only) and filtered values (the Perception Filter reads true state and publishes what a client perceives; presentation nodes read the filtered channel). The kernel exposes `tick_alpha` for render interpolation; owners of moving state expose previous and current committed values in their read views. +**Frame-end delivery and the restore marker** *(New 2026-10-29 — sync knock-on fix; owners ADR-0001 sections 1 and 4, ADR-0004 sections 5 and 6, ADR-0009)*. (1) `Kernel.deliver_frame_end()` first applies deferred subscribe and unsubscribe changes, then closes (sorts) every frame buffer that received a union and delivers each dirty one to the `FRAME_MERGED` classes (`PRESENTATION`, `PROJECTOR`, `DIAGNOSTIC`), then clears them. It is the unconditional last step of `TickDriver.frame()` (CR-1a step 6) and runs exactly once on every exit path: a P6 pause, a restore request, a fault, a zero-tick frame and an ordinary frame (KRN-FRAME-END). The phrases "after the frame's last tick" and "at the exit" in this rule therefore mean "at `deliver_frame_end`", never from P5 and never at the end of the tick loop; `PER_TICK` classes (`INPUT_SURFACE`, `REPLICATION`) are still delivered from P5. A restore frame still runs 0 ticks (CR-1a), so the `deliver_all` batches arrive in the same frame's boundary service, and that frame's `deliver_frame_end` has nothing merged left to deliver. Tested by KRN-FRAME-END and KRN-LOAD-SEQ. **Subscriber lifetime** *(Amended 2026-10-27 — re-review)*: `subscribe(class, handler)` returns a **subscription handle**; `handle.unsubscribe()` removes it, and the kernel also checks `handler.is_valid()` before each call and prunes a freed subscriber (counter `DEAD_SUBSCRIBER`, not an error and not `INCOMPLETE`), so a freed HUD or Chart Table node neve

+**CR-15.
